T21.timing: Bill under 'discusión inmediata'; law expected 17–19 Nov
T21.changed: Truckers' strike (9–12 Nov) ended with a deal: diesel −$142, rises frozen to 31 Mar 2027 (some sources say 7 Apr), cost US$550m–1bn. Bill passed the Chamber Finance committee unanimously on 16 Nov.
T21.problem: A national truckers' strike (9–12 Nov), joined by intercity buses and No+TAG, blocked highways over diesel prices after six consecutive rises. On 15 Nov, 97% had heard of it and about 80% backed it (Cadem, Criteria); 86% found it justified.
T21.politics: The government withdrew its $20 cap bill on 11 Nov and agreed with two truckers' confederations on 12 Nov: diesel −$142 per litre, rises frozen to 31 Mar 2027, wider tax and toll refunds (about US$700m). Independents and No+TAG stayed mobilised. The bill, under 'discusión inmediata', passed the Chamber Finance committee unanimously on 16 Nov; 66% back the measures.

signals.rationale: The truckers' national strike (9–12 Nov) is a focusing event covered by every logged outlet. Polls on 15 Nov show 97% heard of it and about 80% backed it (Cadem, Criteria), so fuel prices stay a top public concern. Level stays 3.

Raised from 2 (W9, after the bill's withdrawal). The government withdrew its $20 cap bill, settled with two truckers' confederations (diesel cut of $142, prices frozen to 31 Mar 2027) and filed the bill with 'discusión inmediata'. The Chamber Finance committee approved it unanimously on 16 Nov and UDI and the opposition back it; 66% support the measures. Law expected 17–19 Nov, so the window is likely to close next week with a decision taken.
Criteria (15 Nov): 79% disagree with keeping Justice Minister Rabat and 72% back his removal; Matthei, from the governing side, called the crisis badly handled. Attention remains high. Level stays 3.

Raised, following the reviewer's note that the accusation is now filed: the opposition filed it on 12 Nov and on 16 Nov the review committee was drawn with a 3–2 opposition majority. This is a formal step with a timetable. Not lowered for coalition arithmetic because the outcome is open: the opposition has about 65 of 78 votes and the PDG caucus (14) is undecided, while UDI says it has no merit and Kast backs Rabat.

Kept at the reviewed level of 2. The Central Bank job-ads index fell for a twelfth month (CIPER, 9 Nov), but, as the reviewer noted, unemployment drew little coverage this week. Q3 GDP (18 Nov) and INE unemployment (27 Nov) are the next tests. Growth and recession talk is now tracked separately as T22.

Criteria (15 Nov): 53% expect job prospects to worsen and 60% expect the economy to worsen (+11). Two outlets report it. No new government move on employment; level held at 2 on mood alone and would drop if nothing follows by W11.

Raised under the reviewer's new budget rule (problem only when there is a cut or a rejection): the Chamber dispatched the budget on 13 Nov after rejecting seven ministry lines and the authorisation to borrow up to US$25bn, which the press called a defeat for the government. Three outlets. Proposed at 3 as a test of the rule; 2 is defensible if this stays a Congress story without public attention.

Hacienda will try to restore the rejected lines in the Senate (17–19 Nov) before the 29 Nov deadline, and added about US$700m for the truckers' deal while defending the consolidation target. A scheduled Senate decision would be level 3; lowered by one because the Chamber vote shows blocking arithmetic and approval is at 18% (the reviewer's lead on executive-driven windows). Same level the reviewer set for W9.

Lowered: the Chamber approved the Health budget 82–41, restored primary-care funds and raised Ricarte Soto funding. With the cuts reversed there is no new event, matching the reviewer's view that this is 'not yet an issue'.
Lowered: the decision was taken in the Chamber; the Senate step remains. Window proposed as closing (decision taken).
The Education line was rejected again (72–72) and stays among the seven rejected lines; under the budget rule a rejection counts as a problem event. Two outlets.
The teachers' union called a national strike and march for 24 Nov over the education budget, and Hacienda offered to restore funds in the Senate. Level 2 (W9 politics is still pending review).

Raised: the truckers' deal doubles the toll refund for intercity buses (35% to 70%), No+TAG joined the blockades demanding lower tolls, and Cadem finds 64% support the refund. Problem stays at 1, so this is watch only.

New topic. The Central Bank expectations survey cut 2026 growth to 0% (10 Nov) and the Finance Minister said Chile is 'technically' in a recession (11 Nov). Indicator change corroborated by the government itself. Q3 GDP on 18 Nov will confirm or ease it.
New topic. Pessimism is rising (60% expect the economy to worsen) and Panel Ciudadano warns of growth without jobs, but there is no government plan or bill on growth. Weak signal.
New topic, weak. The Children's Ombudsman reports more than 41,000 children waiting for protection places and cuts in 102 budget items. One source (CIPER, citing Emol).

The big change the reviewer flagged: approval fell to 18% in Criteria (−6, lowest since taking office) and 27% in Cadem (−2), with Panel Ciudadano near 20%. The fall follows the fuel rise and the strike. Following the reviewer's lead, executive-driven windows were checked: Budget politics is held at 2 rather than 3 because of the Chamber defeat and low approval; the fuel deal (T21) is not lowered because 66% back it; the accusation (T04) is driven by the opposition with 72% support, so it is not lowered either.

stories.title: Approval falls to the lowest of the term
stories.text: Criteria put approval at 18% (−6) and Cadem at 27% (−2) on 15 Nov, after the fuel rise and the truckers' strike. About 80% backed the strike, and 60% expect the economy to worsen.

stories.title: The truckers' deal sets up a fuel law
stories.text: The strike ended on 12 Nov with a $142 diesel cut and prices frozen until March, at a cost of about US$700m. The bill passed the Chamber Finance committee unanimously on 16 Nov, so the window is likely to close this week with a decision.

stories.title: The Chamber rejects seven budget lines
stories.text: Budget 2027 reached the Senate without Education, Interior, Science and four other lines, and without its US$25bn borrowing authorisation. Under the new budget rule this counts as a problem event; the Senate votes 17–19 Nov.
